newsitem.title: USA: Dow snaps 3-day record streak, gyrates with IBM.
newsitem.headline: Dow snaps 3-day record streak, gyrates with IBM.

text.p: U.S. blue chips snapped their three-session record streak as bellwether IBM's quarterly earnings report whipsawed the market and investors took some profits after last week's strong gains.

"It's a fairly quiet week for economic news so it's the quarterly earnings and comments surrounding them that are the news. The market followed IBM. It is certainly a bellwether not just for the tech sector but for corporate America," said Charlie Crane of Spears Benzak Salomon & Farrell.
The Dow industrials lost three to about 6091.

The Dow topped 6100 for the first time intra-day, hitting 6133.73 and then gyrating to a session low of 6059.94. Likewise, IBM ended up 5/8 to 130 after hitting a 52-week high of 135-3/8 and a session low of 126-3/4.

The Dow last week surged 125 points, powered by some solid third quarter earnings reports and firmer bonds. Stocks opened lower on Monday as IBM fell despite reporting third quarter share earnings rose to $2.45, beating the Street's consensus by $0.02. IBM then surged five points during an analysts call with its CFO, who said he was "very comfortable" about 1996 prospects and with IBM's position going forward.
IBM later pared gains as Cowen and Prudential Securities cut its earnings estimates.
The tech-studded Nasdaq Composite lost six to about 1236.
Losers outpaced gainers 13-10 on heavy NYSE volume of about 415 million shares.

"We had a delayed unwinding from (double witching) Friday," said Hildegard Zagorski, a Prudential Securities market analyst. "Techs ran out of steam. They've been up a long way and investors are just backing off here."
Just as IBM set the tone for trading on Monday, Crane, a director of research, said Microsoft could set Tuesday's pace.
Microsoft closed off 3/4 to 134. It reported fiscal quarter earnings of $0.95 a share after the close, up from $0.78 a year ago

As for overall corporate earnings, Crane said, "When the dust settles, most analysts will say earnings were generally better than the most recent expectations. But if we backtracked six to eight weeks they were on target relative to those estimates. Year-over-year comparisons are among the weakest for five years. But the news dominating headlines are those actually registering reasonably respectable earnings."
Oil stocks were mostly flat after several reported results.

Among those exceeding consensus estimates were Texaco, up 2-1/4 to 105-7/8, Chevron, off 3/8 to 67-1/8, and Exxon, off 3/8 to 89, and Amerada Hess on an operating basis, off 1/4 to 55-7/8. Amoco, up 1/2 to 75-3/8, and Mobil, off 1-3/8 to 119-3/4, fell short on an operating basis.

Among other issues, Xerox resumed its slide, off 2-3/8 to 46-1/2 and was the most-active NYSE issue. Lehman Brothers downgraded the stock and Salomon cut earnings estimates. The stock slumped 8-1/8 Friday after a dismal earnings report.
Molten Metal dropped 13-7/8 to 14-1/4 after the Energy Department decided to award it $12 million less than expected.
The company also delayed a Japanese venture. Alex Brown downgraded the stock.

Sinclair Broadcast lost nine to 34-3/4 after warning that it expects proforma broadcast cash flow for its third quarter to be four to five percent below the previous third quarter and revenues to be flat. Alex Brown downgraded the stock.

After the market close, Microsoft said quarterly earnings rose to $0.95, a nickel above consensus. "It's a good number. I would expect stocks to rebound tomorrow," said Philip Orlando, chief investment officer at Value Line Asset Management. The stock rose to 136-3/8 in after-hours trading.
The Nasdaq Composite fell 6.07 to 1236.41.
The S&P 500 index fell 0.97 to 709.85.
(Figures official as of 1645 EDT/2045 GMT)
-- Wall Street desk 212 859 1721
